data.current_description:
Every MCP interaction goes through this single endpoint as a JSON-RPC 2.0 request. It is not a per-tool REST path - the `x-mcp-tools` list on this operation documents the callable tools (name, description, input schema) so an agent can plan a `tools/call` without a live `tools/list` round trip. All tools are read-only.

AUTHENTICATION IS PER-METHOD. The handshake and discovery methods (`initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `resources/list`, `resources/read`) answer with NO token, so an agent can find out what this server is and what it offers before sending a user through OAuth consent. `tools/call` reads a specific user's accounting data and always requires a valid Bearer token; without one it returns 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` header pointing at the RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata. A token that IS presented is always validated, even on a discovery method.
data.summary_suggestion: Execute MCP methods via JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint
data.description_suggestion: Unified JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint for all MCP interactions (discovery, tool execution, resource access). Accepts JsonRpcRequest with method name and parameters; returns JsonRpcResponse with result or error. Authentication is method-specific: discovery methods (initialize, ping, tools/list, resources/list, resources/read) require no token; tools/call requires valid Bearer token and returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate header if missing. All tools are read-only. The x-mcp-tools operation metadata lists callable tools with descriptions and input schemas for agent planning without live discovery round trips.

data.current_description:
Every MCP interaction goes through this single endpoint as a JSON-RPC 2.0 request. It is not a per-tool REST path - the `x-mcp-tools` list on this operation documents the callable tools (name, description, input schema) so an agent can plan a `tools/call` without a live `tools/list` round trip. All tools are read-only.

AUTHENTICATION IS PER-METHOD. The handshake and discovery methods (`initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `resources/list`, `resources/read`) answer with NO token, so an agent can find out what this server is and what it offers before sending a user through OAuth consent. `tools/call` reads a specific user's accounting data and always requires a valid Bearer token; without one it returns 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` header pointing at the RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata. A token that IS presented is always validated, even on a discovery method.
data.summary_suggestion: Execute MCP methods via JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint
data.description_suggestion: Unified JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint for all MCP interactions (discovery, tool execution, resource access). Accepts JsonRpcRequest with method name and parameters; returns JsonRpcResponse with result or error. Authentication is method-specific: discovery methods (initialize, ping, tools/list, resources/list, resources/read) require no token; tools/call requires valid Bearer token and returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate header if missing. All tools are read-only. The x-mcp-tools operation metadata lists callable tools with descriptions and input schemas for agent planning without live discovery round trips.
